blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Analogy focuses on establishing logical relationships between pairs of words, numbers, or symbols.
Classification requires finding the 'Odd One Out' by identifying a shared trait among three options that the fourth lacks.
Number Series tests foundational arithmetic patterns, incremental differences, and common mathematical progressions.
Mastering basic reasoning concepts is essential for scoring quickly in prelims and Tier-1 competitive exams.

Concept:

An analogy tests the ability to identify the relationship between two objects and apply the same relationship to another pair. The relationship can be based on function, category, degree, cause–effect, or part–whole.

Common Types of Analogy in SSC:

1. Object – Function

2. Category – Member

3. Degree / Intensity

4. Cause – Effect

5. Part – Whole

Method to Solve Analogy:

1. Identify the exact relation in the first pair.

2. Apply the same relation to the second pair.

3. Avoid choosing answers based on word similarity alone.

Solved Examples:

Knife : Cut :: Pen : Write

Army : Soldier :: School : Student

Hot : Cold :: Day : Night

items:
Concept:

In classification, four objects are given. Three follow a common rule while one does not. The task is to identify the odd one out.

Basis of Classification in SSC:

• Category

• Function

• Structure

• Property

• Usage
Solved Examples:
Chair, Table, Sofa, Bed → Answer: Bed
Iron, Copper, Gold, Wood → Answer: Wood

Concept:

Number series questions test the ability to identify a pattern in numbers. SBIusually asks simple and moderate level series.

Common Patterns in SSC:

• Addition or subtraction

• Multiplication or division

• Simple progression

• Squares or multiples
Analogy questions often rely on general knowledge pairs like Country-Capital, Quantity-Unit, or Synonym-Antonym.
Always verify that three options strictly share a common rule before classifying the remaining one as the odd one out.
Look for prime numbers, squares, cubes, or alternate arithmetic steps when solving standard Number Series problems.
